title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (2026-03-04)
author: Amina Shah
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product-level overview, PRD highlights, high-level design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family. It is intended for engineering, product, sales engineering, and GTM stakeholders who need a single reference for direction, requirements, and operational constraints.

Summary
- Product name: Unified Inference (UIF)
- Goal: Provide a single developer-facing inference surface across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments with consistent SLOs, deterministic cost controls, and simple rollout mechanics.
- Primary users: software and ML engineers integrating LLM features into products; platform teams standardizing inference; enterprise customers requiring isolation/SLA.

1) Product Overview 
- Core capabilities:
  - Text generation & chat (streams, function/tool calling)
  - Embeddings (batch + streaming)
  - Reranking & structured output
  - Model catalog with vetted performance/quantization profiles
- Differentiators:
  - Unified API across deployment modes
  - Cost-aware routing and batching suggestions (Redwood Optimize integration)
  - Production-first telemetry and rollouts (per-route dashboards, tracing)

2) PRD: Top-level Product Requirements (summary)
- Must-have (MVP):
  1. Single REST/SDK interface for generate/chat/embeddings with consistent request/response shapes.
  2. Model catalog UI + API with metadata: architecture, quantization profile, cost-per-token estimate, latency P50/P95, and compatibility tags.
  3. Per-route SLOs: default latency SLO 100ms P50 for short prompts (<=128 tokens), 300ms P95; configurable per-customer.
  4. Cost controls: per-route token budget, automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when spend threshold reached.
  5. Observability: per-request sampling + token-level cost attribution surfaced in Console and API.
- Should-have (next release):
  - Canary rollouts and automatic rollback based on error rates and quality regressions tied to evaluation prompt sets.
  - Intelligent batching suggestions and automatic prefix caching for repeat prompts.
- Nice-to-have:
  - Per-tenant quantization auto-recommendations and on-the-fly kernel selection hints for Dedicated/Private.

3) Design Specs (high-level)
- API:
  - Endpoint: POST /v1/infer (text generation/chat), POST /v1/embeddings (batch & streaming)
  - Payload examples included in the API spec (see related_pages).
- Runtime behavior:
  - Smart routing policy: route(request) -> evaluate(policy order: customer_pin -> latency_tier -> cost_tier -> region -> fallback model)
  - KV cache: namespace per-route; TTL default 24h; cache hits bypass tokenization + model forward pass for prefix matches.
- Config primitives (config table):
  - route_name: string
  - model_variant: string (e.g., redwood-1.3-quant-cu8)
  - max_tokens_per_request: integer
  - per_minute_qps: int
  - cost_threshold_monthly_usd: integer
  - rollout_policy: one of [stable, canary, a_b_test]

- Ownership: UI/console (Product + DevX), API changes (Eng - serving-runtime), routing & orchestration (Eng - platform), billing hooks (Finance + Eng-infra).

4) Roadmap & Themes (quarterly view)
- Theme Q2 2026: Stable hosting & Dedicated scale
  - Objectives: achieve 99.95% availability for Hosted API; add reserved GPU autoscaling for Dedicated; expose per-route latency SLOs in Console.
  - Milestones: production rollout of canary deploys (2026-04), Dedicated autoscale beta (2026-05).
- Theme Q3 2026: Cost transparency & Optimize integration
  - Objectives: surface token-level cost, model TCO comparisons, Redwood Optimize recommendations in Console.
  - Milestones: Cost attribution GA (2026-07), Redwood Optimize v2 integration (2026-08).
- Theme Q4 2026: Private deployment maturity & enterprise features
  - Objectives: hardened Private control-plane, KMS/HSM integrations, advanced compliance evidence.
  - Milestones: Private on-prem package 1.0 (2026-11), audit logging retention policies (2026-12).

5) Pricing & Packaging Notes (summary)
- Pricing pillars:
  - Usage-based (hosted): per-token generation + per-embedding unit with model-tier multipliers.
  - Reserved capacity (Dedicated): monthly committed spend with baseline throughput guarantees and overage rates.
  - Private: platform fee + optional annual support and professional services.

- Example published pricing (public, USD):
  | SKU                      | Unit        | Base price | Notes |
  |-------------------------|-------------|------------|-------------------------------------------|
  | Hosted-gen-standard     | 1K tokens   | $0.06      | redwood-1.x class, gen workloads           |
  | Hosted-gen-highperf     | 1K tokens   | $0.12      | high-perf model variants, lower latency    |
  | Embeddings-batch        | 1K vectors  | $0.04      | batch optimized embeddings                |
  | Dedicated-reserved-1GPU | monthly     | $6,500     | baseline throughput 1M tokens/day         |

- Packaging guidance for sales:
  - Entry (self-serve): Hosted only, usage pricing, community support.
  - Growth (SMB): Hosted + Dedicated option, committed spend discount, email support.
  - Enterprise: Dedicated or Private, platform fee, advanced SLAs, compliance add-ons.

6) Rollout & Release Notes (v1.0.0 - 2026-03-04)
- Release scope:
  - Public Hosted API for generation and embeddings with model catalog and Console dashboards.
  - Per-route basic cost attribution and latency charts.
  - Beta: Dedicated reserved capacity (invite-only).

- Release highlights:
  1. API: POST /v1/infer supports streaming and function/tool calling. See API examples below.
  2. Console: per-route token breakdown, model catalog with latency & cost estimates.
  3. Billing: per-token invoice line items and monthly usage export.

- Known issues & mitigations:
  - High-concurrency tail latency on long-context requests (>1,024 tokens). Mitigation: automatic fallback to smaller batch size + prioritized routing; engineering ticket SRV-485.
  - Duplicate events in sampling logs when using multi-region routing. Mitigation: dedupe in ingestion pipeline; tracking in infra-queue Q-197.

7) API & CLI Examples
- Generation (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.3","input":"Summarize the following: ...","max_tokens":200,"stream":false}'

- Embeddings (python snippet):
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
  resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-1", inputs=["token1", "token2"])

8) Rollout checklist (for product + eng leads)
  1. Confirm model performance baselines (perf suite run >= 3 days).
  2. Create route in Console with default SLOs and cost threshold.
  3. Canary traffic: 5% for 24 hours, monitor error-rate and quality evals.
  4. If P95 latency increases >30% or eval regression >3% headroom, auto rollback.
  5. Update release notes and notify Customer Success + Sales.

9) Operational and SLOs (summary)
- Availability target (Hosted API): 99.95% monthly.
- Latency targets (default): P50 <= 100ms (<=128 tokens), P95 <= 300ms.
- Error budget policy: 0.05% monthly (SRE owned).
- On-call: Eng-sre rotation; Pager duty escalation per incident runbook.
